question: A 74-year-old man with a history of encephalomyelitis, ataxia, and nystagmus a new diagnosis of small cell carcinoma of the lung (T2, N1, Mn/a) is admitted to the hospital due to painless loss of vision in his right eye. A full workup reveals optic neuritis and uveitis in the affected eye. Which of the following antibodies is most likely to be present in the serum of the patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Small cell carcinoma of the lung -> paraneoplastic syndrome -> autoimmune response -> production of specific antibodies -> Anti-Yo antibody -> 80% CHAIN: Encephalomyelitis, ataxia, and nystagmus -> paraneoplastic syndrome -> specific antibody production -> Anti-Yo antibody -> 75% CHAIN: Optic neuritis and uveitis -> autoimmune etiology -> specific antibody production -> Anti-Yo antibody -> 80%
analysis: Given the patient's history of encephalomyelitis, ataxia, and nystagmus along with the new diagnosis of small cell carcinoma of the lung, the most likely antibody to be present in the serum is Anti-Yo. Anti-Yo antibodies are associated with paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration, which can present with symptoms such as ataxia and nystagmus.
